newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dlr posts gains by close, rallies against AUD.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dlr posts gains by close, rallies against AUD.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer against the Australian and U.S currencies on Thursday and dealers said its break above 65 U.S. cents augured well.
"It's closing on its highs. It's the second upside burst we've seen above 65 cents in the last 24 hours, which is reasonably healthy," said one.

The kiwi traded at US$0.6515/22 and at 64.86 on its Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) by 0500 GMT, up from 0.6486/93 and 64.45 at the open. Against the Australian dollar it rose to A$0.8870/86 from A$0.8788/09 at Wednesday's close.
"There has been a lot of interest in profit-taking on the kiwi/Aussie cross," said the dealer.

"We're not really too sure what the source is behind that -- perhaps just generally healthy demand. But there are rumours a U.S. bank put out a recommendation saying the kiwi is good value against the Aussie at these levels," he said.
Merchandise trade data released early in the session and showing a NZ$150.2 million surplus in the month of June was considered positive for the New Zealand currency.
The kiwi was seen trading in a 0.6500-35 range overnight.
